intent: Eight individual scope and indefinite-pronoun tasks preserve majority, least traffic, fixed-set other, singular another, noun-replacing others and open questions.
picturePurpose: Original complete tools support an explicitly separate fixed-set selection: brush stays out, hammer and scissors go in the cupboard. Coded route counts explain least without claiming real traffic or distance.

transfer.stem: Which summary preserves the workshop notes?
transfer.passage:
Checking the workshop notes
Our club was getting ready for a visitors’ workshop. A note said that most visitors arrived before midday. We kept the meaning of a majority. We did not turn it into all visitors or invent an exact total.
We wanted the route with the least traffic. That meant comparing traffic among the routes, not choosing the shortest distance or assuming there were no vehicles. A separate practice diagram showed vehicle counts at the same moment; those counts were invented for the exercise, not reported road conditions.
At our workbench, the brush was staying out for use. In this separate three-tool example, the hammer and scissors were the other tools to put in the cupboard. The word other modified tools. The note about trying another way to attach the handle suggested a different method, not an already finished handle.
Some pupils drew while others wrote labels. Here others stood for other pupils; the note did not explicitly say every remaining pupil wrote labels. Someone asked, “Does anyone else need a clean brush?” That asked about an additional person. “Has anyone seen the spare key?” and “Can anybody explain the final step?” were questions. They did not identify a person who had seen the key or prove that everyone could explain the step.

options.text: Most means a majority; least traffic need not mean no traffic; others stands for other pupils.
Most means every visitor; least traffic need not mean no traffic; others stands for other pupils.
Most means a majority; least traffic must mean no traffic; others stands for other pupils.
Most means a majority; least traffic need not mean no traffic; others must be followed by pupils.

answer.display: Most means a majority; least traffic need not mean no traffic; others stands for other pupils.
